items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: That's Dee Dee. That's my last spot. ... That's Dee Dee's mother.

ctx.x: I'll watch it there. Yeah, that place looks, I haven't been there for quite a while now.
You all can hardly see this, that's Dee Dee. That's my last spot.
Oh, Dee Dee, yeah, a little baby. How would I take that, really?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: He was playing a ukulele with me at the Kingfish... Me, Dee Dee, Mealy... George, myself, Dee Dee and Mealy. That's what I thought, yeah. The River Bell, yeah.

ctx.x: Well, he was more of an entertainer then. That's it. That's it. Did he play anything at all?

He was playing a ukulele with me at the Kingfish. Start on the ukulele. We had to push him out on the floor. Make him take that yulele on the floor and dance to go mud. You know, that's what he started off. And he'd tell anybody today. He said, Bill and Dee Dee. Start him in that business. Start him in the business. Dance a little, you know. He could dance a little. Then he'd wake yourself up, wake yourself up. He'd wake up in New York. He's back here somewhere. I don't know. I guess back here. He's in the…
Yeah, he's in the absence bar. He always did wake most of the absence bar.
